proof_attempt_summary: The original censor-risk, three-group moment, categorical-information, and headline frontier proofs were closed and verified during this round. Source faithfulness repairs then caused F2 to regenerate three stopped-path transport proof holes, which remain unfinished. tldr: Independent inspections reveal a first-recurrence path through one categorical transition, so increasing the visit count changes information through adjacent transition categories rather than through \(nJ\) independent responses. The proved results establish matching minimax mean-squared-error and uniformly honest connected-interval-length orders \(n^{-1}+\{nJ^2\log(en)\}^{-2/3}\) and \(n^{-1/2}+\{nJ^2\log(en)\}^{-1/3}\) for every \(2\le J\le n^2\). The ambient class imposes terminal Lipschitzness but no class-wide terminal-probability interior floor; the explicit least-favorable traces are instead proved to remain in \([1/4,3/4]\). A fully piecewise complete-death transition statistic attains the frontier without learning the unrestricted death-specific trace. Cross-fitted censor weighting is controlled by an integrated Nelson--Aalen risk bound that uses the censor-survival floor to bound total cumulative hazard and requires neither a pointwise hazard ceiling nor a death-time density. The complete categorical Kullback--Leibler calculation for the specified least-favorable pair gives the rate-level converse.
gap: Fixed-two-visit interval-censoring theory establishes the classical logarithm, and fixed-law mixed-case theory does not expose how its constants evolve when the deterministic visit count grows with sample size. Reversed-mean panel-count methods additionally pool death times through a homogeneous gap function.
fill: The project derives the all-category information modulus, constructs a matching within-person transition estimator, locates the root-\(n\) saturation boundary, and matches the worst-case length of uniformly honest connected intervals under estimated censor survival.
